pathway.title: Arcosa, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The change of control is the dominant credit question: the annual report warns that it could result in a default or prepayment event under each financing document, both note series carry a repurchase offer at 101% of principal on a Change of Control Triggering Event, and no source states what CRH intends for the debt. Repaying the term loan of USD 450.0 million and both note series at 101% would take USD 1,460.0 million, USD 327.9 million more than cash plus the whole USD 700.0 million revolver commitment, so the debt has to be refinanced, waived or left in place with CRH's support. The offer price implies an enterprise value of USD 8,370.6 million, so net debt is 12.00% of the value the buyer is paying, a wide equity cushion if the debt stays in place. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C-21; calculation C-24; calculation C-26

Leverage is moderate at 2.81x total debt and 1.97x net debt on EBITDA of USD 510.6 million for the twelve months to June 2026, but the net figure rests on barge sale cash: only USD 83.0 million of the USD 429.9 million net proceeds, or 19.31%, repaid debt, and of the USD 303.6 million fall in net debt in six months USD 217.5 million is higher cash. This corrects Financial foundation, which subtracted the segment operating profit of USD 46.1 million for the barge business instead of the USD 60.8 million the annual report states and so overstated EBITDA by USD 14.7 million; before the sale proceeds the ratios at 31 March 2026 were 3.02x and 2.71x, not 2.93x and 2.63x. The same error put the barge business at 13.48% of 2025 operating profit in Source readiness, against 17.78%. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C-05; calculation C-06; calculation C-08; calculation C-10; calculation C-20; calculation C-28

Earnings growth since 2025 comes from gains, not trading: EBITDA for the twelve months is USD 14.0 million, or 2.82%, above 2025 without the barge business, yet first-half EBITDA before other operating income was USD 223.2 million against USD 223.1 million a year earlier, because gains on asset sales rose from USD 5.8 million to USD 19.7 million. Segment operating profit rose 14.99%, led by Engineered Structures, but corporate costs rose 43.59% on acquisition and divestiture expenses, so first-half operating profit rose only 6.83%; this normalization is Analyst Judgement applied to this reading only and leaves the leverage figures unchanged. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C-04; calculation C-13; calculation C-14; calculation C-15; calculation C-32

Cash generation is the weakest dimension: continuing operations used USD 68.9 million after capital expenditures in the first half of 2026 against USD 43.1 million a year earlier, as capital expenditures rose 70.50% to USD 102.3 million and receivables absorbed USD 140.1 million. The first half is seasonally the weaker period, producing 17.74% of 2025 operating cash flow of all operations, and 2025 operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 175.5 million including the barge business, 31.07% of EBITDA, so the deficit is not by itself a trend, but a second-half recovery is not established and the debt reduction so far came from disposals. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C-18; calculation C-19; calculation C-31

Demand is shifting from wind towers to utility structures, which supports 2026 and leaves a gap from 2028: the wind tower backlog fell 14.40% to USD 537.4 million with 66% due in 2027 and only USD 32.2 million in 2028, while the utility structures backlog rose 49.02% to USD 648.1 million with 71% due in 2026. The tax credit for wind towers ends for sales after 2027 and one customer was 12.2% of 2025 revenue, about 14.07% without the barge business; Construction Products operating profit fell 8.97% in the first half on lower volumes and weaker cost absorption in specialty materials and asphalt while Engineered Structures rose 37.68%, so profit growth now depends on utility structures. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-15; calculation C-17; calculation C-27

Liquidity and the maturity ladder are not near-term constraints: debt falling due is only USD 17.5 million to 2028, all term loan amortization, and cash is 108.03% of the USD 400.0 million of notes due in 2029. The USD 700.0 million revolver matures on 23 August 2028, before those notes, and its undrawn amount and letters of credit at 30 June 2026 are not stated, so liquidity can only be bounded at USD 1,132.1 million; fixed interest on the notes is USD 58.75 million a year, 59.28% of interest expense, so most financing cost does not move with rates. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C-21; calculation C-22; calculation C-23

Financial policy is modest on distributions and active on acquisitions: dividends are USD 0.20 per share a year, USD 4.9 million was paid in the first half and USD 17.5 million went on share repurchases, while three bolt-on acquisitions cost USD 84.7 million in cash after the USD 1.2 billion Stavola purchase in 2024. No sponsor owns the company, and until closing the merger agreement restricts new debt, asset purchases and sales, and some capital spending, which limits added leverage but also management's room to act. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: The utility structures franchise is the clearest strength: a backlog of USD 648.1 million, up 49.02% since the year end and 71% due in 2026, comes from customers focused on grid reliability and sold partly through multi-year alliance contracts, so about USD 460.2 million of revenue is already ordered for the rest of 2026 against USD 456.0 million recognized in the first half; this supports revenue visibility and cash flow in 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-17

Balance sheet repair is a second strength: net debt of USD 1,004.6 million is 1.97x EBITDA, only USD 17.5 million falls due to 2028, and cash of USD 432.1 million exceeds the notes due 2029, which lowers refinancing pressure in the years before a possible change of control. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C-07; calculation C-08; calculation C-22

Local aggregates positions are a third strength: Construction Products is 51.47% of first-half revenue, sold in markets where transport cost limits competing supply, with capacity utilization of 65% in both segments in 2025, which gives room for volume to lift profit without new plants; this supports margin stability. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C-29

The price and structure of the takeover are a fourth strength for creditors: net debt is 12.00% of the implied enterprise value and the buyer has accepted a larger termination fee, in specified circumstances, than the one Arcosa may owe, which supports completion and a wide equity cushion if the debt stays in place. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; calculation C-26

The change of control is the main weakness: each financing document may treat it as a default or prepayment event, the call on liquidity would be USD 1,460.0 million against at most USD 1,132.1 million, and the sources state neither the definitions nor CRH's intentions, so creditor outcomes are decided outside the evidence. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C-21; calculation C-24

The wind tower cliff and customer concentration are the second weakness: backlog fell 14.40%, only USD 32.2 million is due in 2028, the tax credit ends after 2027 and one customer was 12.2% of 2025 revenue, which puts revenue and capacity absorption at risk from 2028. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-17; calculation C-27

Weak cash generation and earnings quality are the third weakness: first-half free cash flow was a deficit of USD 68.9 million, capital expenditures rose 70.50%, and EBITDA before other operating income was flat, so deleveraging has depended on asset sales and the barge proceeds. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C-14; calculation C-18

Opacity is the fourth weakness: ratings, covenant levels, guarantor lists and the July 2026 amendment are not in the sources, and a completed merger would delist the shares and end the filings creditors now use, so monitoring would depend on the debt documents. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; Business & governance (CP-1A)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No new debt was issued in 2026 to the date of the last filing: the most recent issues were the senior notes due 2032 of USD 600.0 million in August 2024 and the USD 698.3 million term loan of June 2025 that refinanced the 2024 term loan, and in the first half of 2026 the company repaid debt, prepaying USD 83.0 million of the term loan in April from the barge sale proceeds. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C-H1

Two sets of debt documents dated in 2026 were not supplied: Amendment No. 3 to the credit agreement dated 29 July 2026, and a Third and a Ninth Supplemental Indenture with the note trustee dated 1 April 2026, the day the barge sale closed; the sources do not say which notes they amend or why. They matter because the credit agreement secures the revolver and term loan and the notes carry a change-of-control repurchase offer, so any change to guarantors, covenants or the trigger would alter creditor protection. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-03-31_aca_aca-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 113–115

The pending merger would make Arcosa a wholly owned subsidiary of CRH Americas, Inc. for USD 150.00 in cash per share, about USD 7,366.0 million; the agreement is not conditional on financing and carries termination fees of USD 372.0 million payable by CRH and USD 260.4 million payable by Arcosa, with an outside date of 21 June 2027 that can extend by up to six months. The quarterly report does not say whether Arcosa's debt would be repaid, assumed or put back, and until closing the merger agreement restricts Arcosa from incurring indebtedness, acquiring or disposing of assets and some capital spending. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C-A1

fields.value: Financial foundation for Arcosa, Inc. (issuer-1739445), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and cover of the consolidated group from FY2023 to the quarter ended 2026-06-30, built only from the four supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Arcosa's net leverage was 1.91x at 30 June 2026 on a continuing-operations basis, but that figure reflects barge sale cash held on the balance sheet, not earnings growth, so the creditor cushion is only as durable as that cash. Only USD 83.0 million of the USD 429.9 million net sale proceeds repaid debt, leaving USD 432.1 million of cash against USD 1,436.7 million of carrying debt, with a pro forma net leverage of 1.92x after the dividend paid on 31 July 2026. Continuing operations used USD 68.9 million of cash in the first half after capital expenditures, and cash interest cover for 2026 cannot be stated because the quarterly reports give no interest paid.

fields.value: Business, ownership, governance and transaction facts for Arcosa, Inc. (issuer-1739445), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is who owns and controls the issuer, what it does, how it behaves as a borrower and what transactions are pending, built from the four supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Arcosa's credit risk now turns on a pending cash takeover by CRH: a change of control could cause a default or prepayment event under the credit agreement and both note indentures, and how the debt will be treated is not established. The operations are diversified and visible: utility structures backlog of USD 648.1 million supports 2026, wind tower backlog of USD 537.4 million fades as tax credits end after 2027, and one customer was 12.2% of 2025 revenue. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, and barge sale cash prepaid only USD 83.0 million of debt. Nothing dated after 5 August 2026 was supplied, so the shareholder vote scheduled for 4 September 2026 and the July amendment to the credit agreement are unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against treating the takeover as the dominant credit risk is that CRH is paying cash with no financing condition and has accepted a reverse termination fee of USD 372.0 million, larger than the USD 260.4 million Arcosa would owe, which points to completion by a strategic owner rather than a leveraged sponsor, and Arcosa holds USD 432.1 million of cash, enough for a 101% offer on the notes due 2029 of USD 404.0 million but not on both series, which would cost USD 1,010.0 million. The view would turn more negative if the debt documents show a Change of Control Triggering Event is likely or if the July 2026 amendment or the merger agreement added leverage or restricted creditors; it would turn positive if they show the notes and loans staying in place on unchanged terms or CRH repaying the credit agreement debt in full.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Arcosa, Inc. (issuer-1739445), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. It combines the four supplied filings with the accepted source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance work, corrects the earnings perimeter of the financial work, and states no rating, recommendation or recovery value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Arcosa's fundamental credit profile is adequate, with net leverage of 1.97x and USD 432.1 million of cash, but the outcome for creditors depends on the pending CRH cash takeover, whose effect on the debt is not established. A change of control could cause a default or prepayment event under the credit agreement and both note indentures, and repaying every instrument at closing would cost USD 1,460.0 million against at most USD 1,132.1 million of cash and revolver commitment. The 1.97x corrects the 1.91x in Financial foundation, whose EBITDA was USD 14.7 million too high; pro forma net debt after the dividend paid on 31 July 2026 is USD 1,007.1 million, also 1.97x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The change of control is the dominant credit question: the annual report warns that it could result in a default or prepayment event under each financing document, both note series carry a repurchase offer at 101% of principal on a Change of Control Triggering Event, and no source states what CRH intends for the debt. Repaying the term loan of USD 450.0 million and both note series at 101% would take USD 1,460.0 million, USD 327.9 million more than cash plus the whole USD 700.0 million revolver commitment, so the debt has to be refinanced, waived or left in place with CRH's support. The offer price implies an enterprise value of USD 8,370.6 million, so net debt is 12.00% of the value the buyer is paying, a wide equity cushion if the debt stays in place.

This corrects Financial foundation, which subtracted the segment operating profit of USD 46.1 million for the barge business instead of the USD 60.8 million the annual report states and so overstated EBITDA by USD 14.7 million; before the sale proceeds the ratios at 31 March 2026 were 3.02x and 2.71x, not 2.93x and 2.63x. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a cautious reading is that creditors sit under a wide cushion at the price the buyer pays: net debt is 12.00% of the USD 8,370.6 million enterprise value implied by the offer, the merger has no financing condition, and CRH has agreed to pay a termination fee of USD 372.0 million in specified circumstances, 5.05% of the equity value, against USD 260.4 million that Arcosa may owe. Cash of USD 432.1 million exceeds the notes due in 2029, nothing else falls due before then beyond USD 17.5 million of amortization, and the filings' own estimates put the notes due 2029 at 98.40% and the notes due 2032 at 104.45% of principal, from quoted prices in a thinly traded market. The view would improve if the debt documents or CRH show the credit agreement debt repaid and the notes staying in place on unchanged terms, or if second-half cash flow after capital expenditures turns positive; it would worsen if a Change of Control Triggering Event is met while liquidity is below the call, if wind tower orders do not refill the 2028 backlog, or if first-half gains on asset sales prove to be the main source of earnings growth.

fields.value: Arcosa is a listed company with no controlling holder or sponsor named, so its financial policy is set by management and a board that a creditor cannot assess from the supplied filings; the proxy statement that would show board, holdings and pay was not supplied. The credit agreement and both note series are guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries that the filings do not name, the revolver and term loan are secured on substantially all personal property while the notes are unsecured, so the priority between them is by security, not by legal entity, as far as the sources state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 113–115; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: If the merger closes, Arcosa becomes a wholly owned subsidiary of CRH and its shares are delisted and deregistered; creditors would then rely on the debt documents for information and on CRH's financial policy, which the sources do not describe. The offer of USD 150.00 per share implies equity of USD 7,366.0 million, and the fees of USD 372.0 million and USD 260.4 million show the buyer's commitment; neither establishes whether the debt is repaid, assumed or put back.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is partly visible and partly cyclical: first-half revenue rose 2.95% to USD 1,230.4 million, with utility structures up 13.72% and wind towers down 20.19%, and Construction Products up only 2.59%, where higher trench shoring revenue was the main driver and single-family housing weakness held back volumes. Utility revenue is supported by alliance contracts and a backlog of USD 648.1 million, wind tower revenue depends on a tax credit that ends after 2027 and on turbine producers, one of which was 12.2% of 2025 revenue, and construction materials depend on public funding, with a new surface transport authorization or an extension expected by the end of 2026, and on mortgage rates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-16; calculation C-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is local for aggregates, because transport cost is high relative to product value, and contractual for structures, because price escalation clauses pass much of the steel cost to customers; competitive bids in utility structures cap price. For creditors that means margin is more resilient to input costs than to volume: a drop in orders or housing starts, not price, is the way revenue durability would fail.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA margin was 20.14% for the twelve months and 19.74% in the first half against 19.15% a year earlier, but the improvement comes from gains on asset sales and Engineered Structures, whose operating margin rose to 18.72% from 14.05%, while Construction Products margin fell to 11.05% from 12.46%. Selling, general and administrative expense rose 16.95% and corporate costs 43.59% on acquisition and divestiture expenses, which hold reported EBITDA down and persist while the merger is pending, so the margin is held up by gains that may not repeat and held down by deal costs that may.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C-11; calculation C-14; calculation C-15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against steel price moves through escalation clauses and flexing between steel types, and capacity utilization of 65% in Construction Products and Engineered Structures leaves room to add volume; they are less defensible against volume loss in wind towers, where fixed plant cost is spread over fewer units, which is the mechanism behind the sensitivity of USD 66.5 million of EBITDA in the downside scenario.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity has risen: capital expenditures were 8.31% of first-half revenue against 5.74% in 2025, and the plant conversions add growth capital, while receivables absorbed USD 140.1 million of cash in the first half and cash interest was USD 103.1 million in 2025. EBITDA converted to 31.07% free cash flow in 2025 including the barge business, and free cash flow of continuing operations was a deficit of USD 68.9 million in the first half; free cash flow available for debt service is therefore not yet established, and capital expenditure flexibility, with dividends of only USD 4.9 million in the half, is the main lever management has.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation C-18; calculation C-19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is regional in aggregates and national in structures: the aggregates industry is highly fragmented and grows by acquisition, which supports local pricing but invites debt-funded roll-up, while structures producers compete on quality and delivery and, for utility work, in competitive bids; the risk to creditors is acquisition spending, not price war.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is low in aggregates, where proximity to demand centres and permitted reserves act as barriers, and moderate in structures, where capacity can be converted, as Arcosa itself is converting wind tower plants; this protects aggregates margins and exposes structures margins to competitors that can also convert.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes is limited for aggregates and asphalt, and recycled aggregates, of which Arcosa is the largest US producer, are a complement; for wind towers the substitute is a change in policy that removes the tax credit, which the 2025 law does for sales after 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is concentrated in wind towers, where turbine producers are the main customers and one was 12.2% of 2025 revenue, and moderate in utility structures, where alliance contracts offset competitive bids; the effect is price and volume pressure on the wind tower line when orders slow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is moderate: steel is the principal material for Engineered Structures, its price fell through 2025, and escalation clauses and flexing between steel types limit the effect on operating profit; supply was sufficient in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy and economic factors are material to credit quality; social and technological factors are not primary drivers on the provided materials. The 2025 law ends the manufacturing credit for wind towers sold after 2027, which sets the date of the wind tower revenue gap, and a new federal surface transport authorization is expected by the end of 2026 or an extension of the current one; interest rates and housing affordability held back residential volumes, with Texas housing permits down about 8% in 2025, which pressures Construction Products volumes. Demand for electricity, including from artificial intelligence projects, supports utility structure orders, which partly offsets the policy loss.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths in credit terms are the utility backlog of USD 648.1 million, net leverage of 1.97x with cash of USD 432.1 million, local aggregates positions with spare capacity, and fixed-rate notes that are 59.28% of interest expense. Weaknesses are the negative first-half free cash flow, earnings growth that comes from gains, concentration in one wind customer and an opaque debt structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C-08; calculation C-14; calculation C-18; calculation C-23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the conversion of wind tower plants to utility structures, which redirects capacity to growing demand, and a buyer with a stronger balance sheet that leaves the debt in place. Threats are the wind tower credit expiry, the change of control provisions in the debt documents, housing weakness in Texas and the loss of public reporting after closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months utility structures, with 71% of the backlog due in 2026 and 20% in 2027, and public infrastructure budgets in Texas and New Jersey are tailwinds, while the shift from wind towers, housing weakness and the merger's conduct restrictions are headwinds; net leverage is likely to stay near its current level unless the proceeds are spent or cash flow improves. Wind tower backlog would sustain 2027 revenue at about the 2025 level, USD 354.7 million against USD 355.2 million, then falls away, which is the first break in the medium-term outlook.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the credit depends on whether utility structures and aggregates volumes replace wind tower profit and whether the owner after the merger keeps the current financial policy; the sources support neither a positive nor a negative conclusion beyond 2027, and that is stated as not established rather than assumed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside begins with the end of the wind tower tax credit after 2027: with only USD 32.2 million of backlog due in 2028 and no replacement orders, wind tower revenue of USD 355.2 million in 2025 falls away, and one customer that was 12.2% of 2025 revenue stops being a source of volume. The first operational break is lost absorption at the wind tower plants, which cuts Engineered Structures margin; the financial transmission is lower EBITDA, and at the Engineered Structures margin of 18.72% the loss is about USD 66.5 million, 13.02% of EBITDA, taking net leverage to 2.26x, total leverage to 3.24x and interest cover to 4.48x with net debt held constant, an illustration that ignores utility growth and is Analyst Judgement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C-15; calculation C-17; calculation C-30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity would not be the first casualty: cash of USD 432.1 million exceeds debt falling due to 2029 of USD 424.5 million, and management can cut capital expenditures, reduce buybacks and dividends of USD 0.20 per share, and redirect plants to utility structures, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress from operations alone. The sharper path is combined: a change of control that triggers prepayment or the 101% offer when the revolver's availability is uncertain, because the call of USD 1,460.0 million would exceed liquidity of at most USD 1,132.1 million. The primary downside path is therefore a change of control that forces refinancing of the credit agreement debt before the wind tower gap shows in earnings, and the observable triggers are the vote and closing dates, any repurchase offer and the 2028 wind backlog.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_aca_aca-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_aca_aca-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C-21; calculation C-22; calculation C-24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Arcosa presents an adequate business profile supported by a utility structures backlog of USD 648.1 million, local aggregates positions and net leverage of 1.97x, but credit quality is constrained by a change of control whose effect on the debt is not established, a wind tower revenue gap from 2028 and earnings growth that comes from gains. Cash-flow durability appears adequate for debt service on the evidence of 2025, weak in the first half of 2026 and not established for the second half. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the debt documents' treatment of the merger, the revolver's availability and its August 2028 maturity, and CRH's financial policy. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the indentures and Amendment No. 3, the vote and closing outcome, any report after June 2026, ratings, and profit by product line. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: a change of control that forces repayment or refinancing of the debt.
